description: Concrete procedural narrative with no figurative language
text: Well, then, said the teacher, you may take your slate and go out behind the schoolhouse for half an hour. Think of something to write about, and write the word on your slate. Then try to tell what it is, what it is like, what it is good for, and what is done with it. That is the way to write a composition. Henry took his slate and went out. Just behind the schoolhouse was Mr. Finney's barn. Quite close to the barn was a garden. And in the garden, Henry saw a turnip. Well, I know what that is, he said to himself; and he wrote the word turnip on his slate. Then he tried to tell what it was like, what it was good for, and what was done with it. Before the half hour was ended he had written a very neat composition on his slate.

description: Text built around abstract qualities and rhetorical idealization
text: Liberty is not a gift bestowed upon the timid. She is a flame kindled in the hearts of those who dare to reach beyond the comfort of obedience, who look upon injustice and refuse to avert their gaze. History has always rewarded the bold — not because boldness guarantees victory, but because it is the only force capable of bending the arc of what is possible. To demand freedom is to already be halfway free.

description: Literal historical narrative with archaic phrasing that creates vagueness for grade 5
text: The settlers rose before dawn to yoke the oxen and load the wagon with their earthly goods. The trail was rutted and treacherous after the autumn rains, and many a wheel sank deep into the mire before the party had traveled half a league. By midday they had forded the creek and made camp on the far bank, grateful that Providence had seen fit to spare them further hardship for one day.
